note: Same prospect as the 26 May call, re-assessed with the financial picture now visible. Matches successful: runs his own company, describes himself as a dealmaker who makes deals 'all day', provides for his family — though he resists the word himself, 'it's not like successful, but I think I'm in a good way.' Matches income, which was unresolved on the first call and is now answerable: he is in Denmark on what he calls a good salary and a good lifestyle, called $9,000 'a lot of money' rather than impossible, and agreed to $6,000 on a monthly schedule without any claim of inability to pay. That is a pass on affordability, and it is the difference between this prospect and the Badrane Hriouch edge case, who was anchored at $200 a month. Matches neglected_health on the same reading applied to the Francisco Vega assessment: health is the neglected area of an otherwise functioning life, degraded across a decade of 70% seated days rather than by an acute event — close to the crisis boundary given a compressed disc, a subluxing knee and two years of hypertension, but presenting as accumulated neglect. Matches not_deconditioned: roughly 15 kg above his own target rather than the 50 lb the exclusion names, and decisively not gym-averse in the sense the criterion means — he trained heavily last year, bought kettlebells unprompted, and planned to train immediately after this call. Misses good_to_great, and this remains the single material miss: he is not going from good to great, he is trying to return to a self he last inhabited fourteen years ago, and his own framing is a decline narrative — 'I think I'm heading downwards in this game at this point. And I will be more and more weak.' Edge rather than core on that one criterion. The wider finding, consistent across this batch: good_to_great is doing most of the exclusion work against prospects who otherwise fit the definition precisely and are willing to pay. This prospect passes four of five, shook hands on $6,000, and would be excluded on the criterion the ICP quote leans on hardest. Judged on criteria, not outcome — the call ended in a follow-up over vendor verification, not over fit.
